text:
julie-accounting: FYI customer 'Nordic Ware' — invoice #98765 failed when we tried to charge the company card for TransitCorp booking. Customer says vendor needs payment today. Gateway returned decline_code: merchant_block. Any quick ideas?

sara-support: Can you paste the gateway error + last4/token? Also is this the corporate card tied to the customer's billing profile?

julie-accounting: Pasting redacted gateway response: ```{
  "error": "card_declined",
  "decline_code": "merchant_block",
  "mcc": "4722",
  "issuer_message": "cardholder's plan blocks travel merchants",
  "approved": false
}``` Last4: 4242, token: tok_abc123 (billing profile: nordic-987). Cardholder monthly spend_limit_cents: 50000 (€500) attempted charge: 65000 (€650).

mike-payments: Two separate failure signals: 1) issuer-level MCC block (merchant_block) 2) attempted amount > card's monthly spend limit. Issuer is explicitly blocking MCC 4722 (travel). If customer can't change issuer policy immediately, options: different card, bank phone-override, or virtual card with different MCC profile.

kevin-engineering: Also flagged in our logs: we fall back to 3DS auth and the gateway returned a 502 during auth flow earlier — snippet from our calllog: 
```
POST /v1/payments/auth3d tok_abc123 -> 502 gateway-timeout (2026-03-17T09:02:11Z)
Retry -> 200 auth_challenge_required
```
If the 3DS challenge fails, issuer may decline even if MCC allowed. So both MCC and auth instability could be contributing.

julie-accounting: Customer response: they cannot add a different card quickly (company policy) and they also require a PO attached to the invoice so switching to manual ACH is possible but slow. They asked if we can re-run the charge after lowering the amount to within limits or issuing a partial payment.

sara-support: We can't alter a customer's card limit. We can: 1) attempt a smaller charge (partial capture) if the vendor accepts split payments, 2) request customer to contact their issuing bank to allow MCC 4722 for this merchant, or 3) offer manual bank transfer / ACH. Suggest escalating to billing ops for manual options. @anna-billing @mike-payments can you advise? :pray: 

anna-billing: On it. Manual options: we can issue an invoice with bank transfer instructions (SEPA) immediately — that avoids card entirely. We can also schedule a one-off retry attempt in 24h but we need explicit written authorization from the cardholder to retry a declined charge (audit requirement). If they insist on card payment today, they'd need to contact the issuer for a phone authorization (we cannot supply PAN/CVV).

payment-gateway-bot: [automated] Charge retry attempted at 2026-03-17T09:20:43Z for token tok_abc123 -> decline: do_not_honor (decline_code: do_not_honor).

mike-payments: Noted. The do_not_honor could be issuer refusing because of MCC mismatch or because of exceed_limit. Either way, best path for same-day is manual bank transfer. If the customer can arrange a temporary increase or unblock with their bank (sometimes a 5-min phone call), we can reattempt once confirmation received. Also logging note: open an internal postmortem ticket for the 3DS 502 occurrences — tagging @kevin-engineering.

kevin-engineering: Filing a follow-up on 3DS instability. I’ll pull gateway traces and correlate with region (EU). Might be a transient gateway hiccup.

julie-accounting: Customer accepted SEPA transfer and will pay today. They asked if we can mark the invoice as 'processing' while funds arrive so vendor doesn't get blocked. @anna-billing?

anna-billing: Yes — we'll set the invoice status to pending-payment and notify the vendor to proceed on good faith. I'll document the customer's bank transfer reference when it arrives and reconcile. Closing escalation on our side once funds clear.

julie-accounting: Thanks everyone — closing ticket. :white_check_mark:
